title: Times and dates
grammar: Prepositions of time and time expressions
summary: om + clock time, op + day or date, in + month, season, year. over een uur = from now; twee jaar geleden = ago. sinds and al take the present for what is still going on. half drie is 2.30.
explain:
English and Dutch both use small words to place things in time, but they do not always choose the same ones: "in an hour" is `over een uur`, "three years ago" is `drie jaar geleden`. Most of them are fixed pairs that you learn once and then use every day: for opening hours, appointments and dates.

### om, op, in

| | use it for | example |
| om | a clock time | om drie uur |
| op | a day, a date | op maandag, op 5 mei |
| in | a month, season, year | in mei, in de zomer, in 2020 |

> De bibliotheek gaat om half negen open. — The library opens at half past eight.
> Op feestdagen sluit de winkel al om vier uur. — On public holidays the shop already closes at four.
> In de zomer zijn de openingstijden anders. — In the summer the opening hours are different.

Also with in: `in het weekend`, `in de ochtend`. For parts of the day the short forms are more usual: `'s morgens` or `'s ochtends`, `'s middags`, `'s avonds`, `'s nachts`. A day without op (`Ik werk maandag`) means this coming or this past Monday; `op maandag` can also mean every Monday.

### No preposition

With `vandaag`, `morgen`, `gisteren`, `vorige week`, `volgend jaar`, `deze week`, `dit jaar`, `elke dag`, `afgelopen zaterdag` there is no preposition: `Ik heb volgende week vrij`, never *in volgende week.

### From now, ago, how long

- `over` = from now: `over een uur`, `over twee weken`.
- `geleden` = ago, and it comes **after** the time: `twee jaar geleden`.
- `binnen` = within: `binnen een week`.
- `voor` and `na` = before and after: `voor het werk`, `na de les`.
- `tot` = until; `van … tot` = from … to (on signs: `tot en met`, up to and including); `tussen … en` = between; `vanaf` = from … on; `tijdens` = during.
- `rond` and `tegen` = about, around: `rond tien uur`, `tegen vijf uur`.

> De vergadering begint over een kwartier. — The meeting starts in a quarter of an hour.
> Ik heb de afspraak twee weken geleden verzet. — I moved the appointment two weeks ago.

### sinds and al: the present tense

For something that started in the past and is **still going on**, Dutch uses the **present** tense: `sinds` + a starting point, or `al` + a length of time.

> Ik woon sinds 2021 in Nederland. — I have been living in the Netherlands since 2021.
> Hij werkt hier al drie jaar. — He has been working here for three years.

The perfect `Hij heeft hier drie jaar gewerkt` means that he no longer works here.

### pas and al

`al` = already, earlier than expected; `pas` = not until, later than expected.

> De bus komt pas over twintig minuten. — The bus is not coming for another twenty minutes.

### The clock and dates

Dutch counts the half hour towards the **next** hour: `half drie` is 2.30. Around it: `kwart over twee` (2.15), `tien voor half drie` (2.20), `vijf over half drie` (2.35), `kwart voor drie` (2.45). For 2.20 and 2.40 you also hear `twintig over twee` and `twintig voor drie`.

Dates: `op 1 mei`, spoken `op één mei` or `op de eerste mei`. The ordinal ends in **-ste** for 1, 8 and from 20 on (`eerste`, `achtste`, `twintigste`), and in **-de** for the others (`tweede`, `derde`, `negende`, `twaalfde`). The date question is `De hoeveelste is het vandaag?`

> De hoeveelste is het vandaag? — What is the date today?

### Watch out

- From now is over, not in: `over een uur`, not *in een uur.
- Still going on: `Ik woon hier sinds 2021`, not *Ik heb hier sinds 2021 gewoond.
- A date takes op: `op 15 mei`, not *in 15 mei.
- `half drie` is 2.30, not 3.30.

### Compared with Ukrainian

Two things work as in Ukrainian: `пів на третю` is `half drie`, and `тому` comes after the time just like `geleden`: `два роки тому`, `twee jaar geleden`. And Ukrainian also uses the present for "since": `Я живу тут з 2021 року` is `Ik woon hier sinds 2021`.

sentences.nl: De bibliotheek gaat om half negen open.
sentences.en: The library opens at half past eight.
sentences.note: om before a clock time. Half negen is half an hour before nine, so 8.30, not 9.30.
alt: Om half negen gaat de bibliotheek open.
De bibliotheek opent om half negen.
Om half negen opent de bibliotheek.

sentences.nl: Op feestdagen sluit de winkel al om vier uur.
sentences.en: On public holidays the shop already closes at four o'clock.
sentences.note: op before a day, om before the clock time. Al says it is earlier than you might expect.
alt: De winkel sluit op feestdagen al om vier uur.

sentences.nl: In de zomer zijn de openingstijden anders.
sentences.en: In the summer the opening hours are different.
sentences.note: in before a season, with the article: in de zomer. The same with months and years, without article: in juli, in 2025.
alt: De openingstijden zijn in de zomer anders.

sentences.nl: De vergadering begint over een kwartier.
sentences.en: The meeting starts in a quarter of an hour.
sentences.note: English 'in' for time from now is over in Dutch: over een kwartier. In een kwartier would mean 'within', how long something takes.
alt: Over een kwartier begint de vergadering.

sentences.en: I have been living in the Netherlands since 2021.
sentences.note: I still live here, so Dutch uses the present tense with sinds, where English uses 'have been living'.

sentences.nl: Hij werkt hier al drie jaar.
sentences.en: He has been working here for three years.
sentences.note: al + a length of time, with the present: he still works here. Hij heeft hier drie jaar gewerkt would mean he has left.
alt: Hij werkt al drie jaar hier.

sentences.nl: Ik heb de afspraak twee weken geleden verzet.
sentences.en: I moved the appointment two weeks ago.
sentences.note: geleden comes after the length of time: twee weken geleden. Here the action is finished, so the perfect is right.
alt: Twee weken geleden heb ik de afspraak verzet.
Ik heb twee weken geleden de afspraak verzet.

sentences.nl: Het concert duurde tot elf uur 's avonds.
sentences.en: The concert lasted until eleven o'clock in the evening.
sentences.note: tot = until. 's avonds is the usual way to say 'in the evening'; it comes after the clock time here.
alt: Het concert duurde tot 's avonds elf uur.

sentences.note: The fixed question for the date: de hoeveelste, from the ordinal numbers. Vandaag needs no preposition.

sentences.nl: De bus komt pas over twintig minuten.
sentences.en: The bus is not coming for another twenty minutes.
sentences.note: pas = not until, later than you would like. Over twintig minuten counts from now.

exercises.nl: Volgens het rooster begint de les ___ tien uur.
exercises.en: According to the timetable the lesson starts at ten o'clock.
exercises.note: A clock time takes om. Op is for days and dates, in for months, seasons and years.

exercises.nl: Volgens mijn agenda is de afspraak ___ 3 juni.
exercises.en: According to my diary the appointment is on 3 June.
exercises.note: A date takes op, like a day: op 3 juni, op maandag. In is only for the whole month: in juni.

exercises.nl: Je bent op tijd: de film begint pas ___ tien minuten.
exercises.en: You are on time: the film does not start for another ten minutes.
exercises.note: Counting from now is over: over tien minuten. In tien minuten is the English pattern, not Dutch.

exercises.nl: Ze heeft de les twee dagen ___ geannuleerd.
exercises.en: She cancelled the lesson two days ago.
exercises.note: 'Ago' is geleden, and it comes after the time: twee dagen geleden. Sinds means since, a starting point.

exercises.nl: ___ de lunchpauze is de balie gesloten.
exercises.en: During the lunch break the desk is closed.
exercises.note: tijdens = during, for the whole period of something. Om only goes with a clock time.
Half elf is 10.30, and 10.20 is ten minutes before that: tien voor half elf. Tien over half elf is 10.40.
Dutch counts the half hour towards the next hour: 7.30 is half acht, half an hour before eight.

exercises.nl: Op werkdagen zijn we ___ negen tot vijf uur open.
exercises.en: On working days we are open from nine to five.
exercises.note: From … to is van … tot; vanaf … tot is also heard. Tot without van would just mean until.

exercises.en: The meeting is on the eighth.
exercises.note: Acht is one of the numbers that take -ste, like eerste and twintigste. Most others take -de: tweede, negende.

exercises.nl: De winkel gaat ___ om tien uur open, niet om negen.
exercises.en: The shop does not open until ten o'clock, not at nine.
exercises.note: pas = not until, later than expected. Al would say the opposite: earlier than expected.

answers: Ik woon hier al vijf jaar.
Ik woon al vijf jaar hier.
exercises.en: I have been living here for five years.
exercises.note: The present tense with al + a length of time, because you still live here. English needs 'have been living'.

answers: Morgen ben ik om drie uur bij de tandarts.
exercises.en: Tomorrow I am at the dentist's at three o'clock.
exercises.note: Morgen needs no preposition. In the middle of the sentence the time comes before the place: om drie uur bij de tandarts.

exercises.task: Say the time the way people speak, with half.
answers: De film begint om half negen.
De film begint om half negen 's avonds.
exercises.en: The film starts at half past eight.
exercises.note: 20.30 is 8.30 in the evening, and Dutch counts towards the next hour: half negen.

exercises.en: I have been living here since 2020.
exercises.note: You still live here, so Dutch uses the present tense with sinds. The perfect would mean that you have moved away.

exercises.wrong: Mijn dochter is in 15 mei geboren.
answers: Mijn dochter is op 15 mei geboren.
exercises.en: My daughter was born on 15 May.
exercises.note: A date takes op, just like a day of the week. In is for the month alone: in mei.

exercises.wrong: De dokter belt je in een kwartier terug.
answers: De dokter belt je over een kwartier terug.
De dokter belt je binnen een kwartier terug.
exercises.en: The doctor will call you back in a quarter of an hour.
exercises.note: From now is over: over een kwartier. Binnen een kwartier (within) is also right. In een kwartier is copied from English.
